newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU leaders to weigh Middle East peace appeal.
newsitem.headline: EU leaders to weigh Middle East peace appeal.

text.p: European Union leaders will consider an appeal to the peoples of the Middle East to press their governments to resume stalled peace negotiations at a summit in Amsterdam this week, diplomats said on Sunday.

They said France had offered a draft statement, voicing deep concern at the impasse in the Arab-Israeli peace process and at the potential threat to peace, which EU foreign ministers would study on Monday night and leaders could issue on Tuesday.

The declaration would urge all sides to resume negotiations on the basis of the principles of exchanging of land for peace, the right of peoples to self-determination and the right of all to security.

It would declare the willingness of the European Union, alongside the United States and other states of the region, notably Egypt, to help promote a resumption of talks between Israel and the Palestinian Authority.
Hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cancelled a planned trip to the United States on Saturday in an apparent sign of deadlock over the resumption of peace talks.
Clashes between Palestinian youths and Israeli soldiers erupted for the second day running in the West Bank city of Hebron amid worsening violence.
The EU sent a 10-point plan for measures to resume the Arab-Israeli dialogue to the United States two months ago but has not yet received a formal reply.

The plan, contained in a letter from Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierloo to U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, advocated a series of confidence-building measures, including a freeze on a disputed Israeli settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Under the EU plan, all sides would agree not to break off talks due to acts of violence and to cooperate fully in the fight against terrorism.
Diplomats said that in a concession to Israeli Prime Minister Bejamin Netanyahu, the EU draft proposed bringing forward negotiations on the final status of the Palestinian territories.
But it would also require Israel to freeze settlements and end an economic blockade on the West Bank and Gaza Strip, allowing the construction of a port and an airport in Gaza.

Diplomats said German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel had expressed some reservations about the draft appeal in talks with French Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine on Friday in Poitiers but they said other countries had no major differences on the text.
